encoding: 8-bit greyscale, value = clamp(floor((elev_m + 6000) / 12000 * 255 + 0.5), 0, 255); decode elev_m = value / 255 * 12000 - 6000 (step 47.06 m). Sea level (0 m) maps to 127.5 exactly; with round-half-up, value 127 covers [-47.06, 0) m and value 128 covers [0, +47.06) m, so value >= 128 <=> elev >= 0 m (land) and value <= 127 <=> elev < 0 m (sea). In a shader (texel = value/255): land = texel >= 0.5. Elevations beyond -6000/+6000 m are clamped (source range is about -9000..+6000 m). Each slice is 512x256 equirectangular, lon -180 at left edge to +180 at right edge, lat +90 at top edge to -90 at bottom edge, pixel centres at half-pixel offsets; bilinearly resampled from the 1 deg grid. Slices are stacked vertically in 'index' order: slice i occupies rows [256*i, 256*i+255] of the 512 x (256*N) image.
source: Scotese, C.R., Wright, N., 2018, PALEOMAP Paleodigital Elevation Models (PaleoDEMS) for the Phanerozoic, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.5460860 (1deg x 1deg netCDF v2), CC BY 4.0
